name: Dograh

hlido_opinion.headline: Open-source, self-hostable voice-agent platform positioned squarely as the Vapi/Retell alternative — unusually broad provider matrix and a genuine air-gapped story, but the voice quality and privacy claims are untested on the public surface.
hlido_opinion.body: Dograh makes the sharpest positioning bet in the voice-agent space right now: it is the fork-it-yourself, run-it-on-your-own-infrastructure answer to the hosted incumbents (Vapi, Retell). The public surface backs the pitch with substance rather than slogans — a visual workflow builder where every stage of the pipeline (inbound channel, STT, LLM, TTS, telephony) is a swappable node, and a genuinely long list of interchangeable providers (Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Groq, OpenRouter, Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, Asterisk, and dozens more), plus a speech-to-speech path that skips the cascade entirely. The BSD-2 license and 5.5k+ GitHub stars make the open-source claim credible, and the Product Hunt #1-of-day/week recognitions and NVIDIA Inception listing are real external signals. The load-bearing differentiator — 'your data never leaves', deploy on-prem or air-gapped so no calls, recordings, transcripts or model inference cross your boundary — is exactly what a regulated buyer wants, and exactly what cannot be confirmed from a marketing page: it is a claim to verify in a deployment, not a fact we observed. For an agentic ecosystem, the appeal is that a coding agent (the site names Claude Code, Cursor, and others) can reportedly spin up and modify agents against your own stack. Treat that, too, as an advertised capability pending hands-on confirmation. The honest read: a serious, well-differentiated OSS project with strong momentum, reviewed here only at the surface.

tier_rationale: STEADY (76): the product is clearly articulated, the feature surface is deep and specific (not vaporware bullet points), the open-source license and traction signals are verifiable, and the positioning fills a real gap (self-hosted/air-gapped voice agents). Held below the top band because the defining claims — voice quality, latency, and the air-gapped/no-data-egress guarantee — are unverified at Tier-1, pricing for the hosted 'Try Cloud' tier was not captured, and a young high-velocity project carries more roadmap risk than the established hosted incumbents.
what_it_does_well: Sharp, credible positioning as the self-hostable OSS alternative to Vapi/Retell
Genuinely broad, swappable provider matrix across STT, LLM, TTS and telephony
Visual workflow builder plus a speech-to-speech path for lower-latency pipelines
Open-source (BSD-2) with strong external traction signals (5.5k+ stars, Product Hunt #1)
On-prem / air-gapped deployment story that hosted incumbents structurally cannot match
what_it_fails_at: Core voice quality, latency and reliability are untested on the public surface
The headline 'data never leaves / air-gapped' guarantee is advertised, not verified here
Hosted 'Try Cloud' pricing and limits were not captured at Tier-1
Young, fast-moving project — API/feature stability and long-term maintenance are unproven
Agent-runtime integration (Claude Code/Cursor spinning up agents) is a claim, not a tested path
best_for: Teams that need voice agents inside their own VPC or fully air-gapped for compliance
Engineering orgs that want to own and fork the stack rather than rent a hosted API
Builders who want to swap STT/LLM/TTS/telephony providers without re-platforming
Anyone evaluating an OSS exit from Vapi/Retell lock-in
not_recommended_for: Teams that want a fully managed, zero-ops hosted voice API and nothing to run
Buyers who need a vendor with a long production track record today
Use cases that require an independently benchmarked voice-quality/latency guarantee before commit

compared_to.verdict_diff: Vapi is the polished hosted incumbent with a longer track record; Dograh is the self-hostable OSS challenger. Choose Vapi for zero-ops managed infrastructure; choose Dograh when data residency, forking, or air-gapped deployment is the constraint.
Retell is another strong hosted voice-agent platform. Dograh's pitch is explicitly the open-source alternative to it — same problem space, opposite deployment philosophy.
Bland is hosted and phone-call-focused. Dograh trades turnkey convenience for provider flexibility and on-prem control.

evidence_urls.claim: Positions as open-source, self-hostable alternative to Vapi & Retell
Swappable pipeline (STT/LLM/TTS/telephony) with a broad provider matrix
Data never leaves your boundary / on-prem / air-gapped inference
Point Claude Code/Cursor/agent runtimes at it to build & deploy agents

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Self-hosted voice-agent platform with a workflow builder and provider-pluggable pipeline; the vendor claims agent runtimes (Claude Code, Cursor) can build and deploy agents against it. Behaviourally testable in a deployment, though not exercised at Tier-1.
